chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who partnered with another man in a female slave, and he said to him: 'If you gain profit, it is yours, and if you incur a loss, there is no liability upon you.' He (the Imam) said: 'There is no objection to that if the female slave belongs to the one who speaks.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a profit-only partnership in a female slave to be valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the flexibility of classical Islamic partnership contracts (mudarabah-style arrangements) regarding risk allocation, specifically validating a scenario where one partner assumes all loss liability while sharing profit. The condition that the asset must belong to the risk-bearing partner highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on clear ownership and the absence of gharar (uncertainty) in such commercial agreements. It serves as a foundational precedent for modern Islamic finance structures involving asymmetric risk and reward distribution.
